A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same functional longitudinal causal-inference framework, despite the changed title and contribution framing. The complete main texts, figures, table, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical identification results and proofs. Figure 1 illustrates possible stochastic trajectories, the clinical examples are motivating applications, and Section 5 discusses future estimation and simulation rather than reporting empirical study outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical, including its appendix. Figure 1 retains the illustrative trajectories, the clinical examples contain no original analyses, and Section 5 explicitly leaves empirical estimation and numerical studies to future work.

M1.justification: The g-computation, IPW, doubly robust formulas, and prospective estimation approach are retained. Section 4 revises their censored target-measure construction: v3 conditions event and covariate factors on remaining uncensored and changes the censoring indicators. Outcome processes, death, and censoring were already accommodated in v2.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates the framework on datasets or tasks. The change from MIMIC-III to MIMIC-IV in the ICU example updates a motivating application, without reporting actual dataset use.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated comparison methods. The methods discussed in Section 2 and Table 1 are literature classifications, not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version provides an executed evaluation protocol, experimental sample sizes, budgets, or evaluation metrics. Section 5.1 retains a prospective estimation scheme based on increasingly fine partitions and possible pre-smoothing.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, or analyzed clinical case studies. Sensitivity analysis and investigations of discrete observation remain future directions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The discussion of double robustness concerns theoretical identification properties.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries or performance comparisons to update. Figure 1 retains the same illustrative trajectories; the added Figure 2 depicts conceptual relationships rather than new empirical findings.

T1.justification: Assumptions 6 and 6′ change from conditions on the joint family of counterfactuals to uniform bounds on individual treatment-regime counterfactual laws. Section 4 revises the censored target measure and separates outcome consistency in Assumption 3′ from full covariate consistency in the added Assumption 7′. The appendix removes the explicit unprimed Theorems 1–4 and Proposition 6 proofs, retains Theorem 7's proof, and adds explicit proofs of Theorems 1′, 2′, and Proposition 6′.

C1.justification: v2 presents the unified identification framework as its principal new contribution. v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion recast the paper as an extension and fuller exposition of Ying (2024), emphasizing outcome processes, death/censoring, formal justification, and interpretability. Much of that substantive coverage already existed in v2, but the claimed contribution and attribution change substantially.

C2.justification: v3 adds a collider/confounding explanation in Section 2.1 and explicitly asserts population bias from directly applying existing approaches in Section 2.3. Section 5.2 expands the rationale for deferring estimation and removes v2's prediction of both model and rate double robustness for future estimators. The principal positivity, continuity, and discretization limitations remain.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies an implemented estimator, reproducible experimental configuration, or code release. The partition-based estimation and pre-smoothing suggestions in Section 5.1 remain a conceptual blueprint, without added implementation or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Ying (2024) becomes the explicit foundation throughout the abstract, Section 3, Table 1, and appendix, substantially changing novelty positioning and attribution. v3 also adds references including Pearl (2009), Johnson et al. (2023), and Klonoff et al. (2017), while removing citations such as Smucler et al. (2019) and Zhang and Wang (2016).

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, literature review, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Literature material moves from Section 1 into Section 2, motivating examples move into the preliminaries, and Section 3 gains a separate conceptual overview and reordered subsections.

P2.justification: v3 broadly redesigns the document's typography, title block, headings, running headers, equation-number placement, and reference layout. It adds the nested-category diagram in Figure 2 and relocates Table 1 from the introduction to Section 2.4. Figure 1 retains its plots but adds reproduction attribution.

improvement.justification: v3 adds explanatory material and explicit censored-case proofs where v2 largely referred to analogous arguments, but removes several foundational proofs. It also leaves an unresolved formal mismatch: Assumption 3′ now covers outcomes rather than all covariates, yet Proposition 6′ and its proof still invoke it instead of the separately stated strong consistency Assumption 7′. These benefits and unresolved dependencies prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
